note: Terms module-02 introduces, and the lesson responsible for teaching each. Enforced by scripts/lint-glossary.mjs: a lesson may not use a term before the lesson that teaches it. Written 2026-08-22 after the owner - the product owner - could not read this module's own vocabulary. Beacon carried the worst load in the curriculum: three-way match used 17 times, tolerance 23, PO 18, receipt 20, and not one of them defined anywhere. Keep ASCII-only.

terms.gloss: Purchase order: the promise the company made before anything arrived - what was ordered, how many, at what price.
The proof the goods actually showed up, and how many. Separate from the bill on purpose: one says what was promised, one says what arrived.

Checking the invoice against the PO and the goods receipt before paying: right item, actually arrived, right price. You do this yourself when a couch is delivered - order confirmation, delivery slip, bill.
How big a price or quantity gap is allowed to pass without a human looking. Small gaps are normal (freight, rounding); the tolerance is where someone drew the line, on purpose.
A vendor billing more than was agreed. Some gaps are innocent; an overcharge is the kind you claw back.
Money recovered after it was already paid - the expensive way to catch an overcharge, and the reason the tolerance exists.
Accounts payable: the desk that pays what the company owes suppliers.
The governed list of who the company is allowed to pay, and where the money goes. Changing a bank detail here is the single highest-risk edit in the whole workflow.
The same bill arriving twice - usually a resend, occasionally fraud. Paying it twice is real money out the door.
An invoice the rules could not clear on their own, parked where a person will work it. An exception is a routing outcome, not a failure.
An invoice that clears every check and moves toward payment with no human touching it. Straight-through means no manual work, not no controls.
One batch of approved invoices paid together at a cutoff, rather than one payment at a time. One approval covers the batch.
The note sent to a vendor saying which invoices a payment covers, so they can match the money to their own records.
Business email compromise: an attacker posing as a vendor to change the bank details on file. The reason a bank-detail change needs a second approver and an out-of-band callback.
